grade.first_issue: The claim that the terminal set S_p^* contains the single element v_p(M) is false when p does not divide M; then S_p^* is empty.
grade.summary: The termination argument and the primewise gcd invariant are correct and establish both conclusions. The only defect is an omitted empty-set case for primes not dividing M. Since the solution explicitly defines the gcd of an empty S_p^* as 0, the argument is repaired immediately by splitting into p dividing M and p not dividing M.
strengths: Correctly shows that the product is unchanged when gcd(m,n)=1 and strictly decreases otherwise.
Correctly shows that gcd-one moves reduce the number of entries greater than 1, yielding termination.
Correctly proves that at least one entry greater than 1 always remains.
Correctly identifies the valuation transformation as (x,y) to (min(x,y),|x-y|).
Correctly establishes invariance of the gcd of the positive p-adic valuations and reconstructs M from these invariants.

errors.description: For p not dividing the terminal integer M, the positive-exponent multiset is empty, not a singleton containing 0. The stated convention gcd(empty)=0 supplies the missing case directly.
